outcomes: Application code uses one object API while composition selects memory, filesystem, S3, GCS, or managed bindings
Logical buckets and key prefixes isolate application data from provider bucket names
The plugin-provided backend rejects disallowed or oversized uploads to registered buckets, and a rejected upload leaves the existing object intact
Control-plane deadlines do not truncate a streaming object body after Get returns
nonGoals: Providing cross-backend transactions or automatic replication
Making a backend you construct yourself enforce bucket constraints unless you wrap it
Bounding the size of an upload made through a signed PUT URL
Granting signed URLs without both backend capability and binding permission

requirements.text: Backends implement put, get, delete, list, exists, copy, and close consistently; a missing Get returns no object and no fabricated content; a Put whose body reader fails commits nothing and leaves any existing object intact.

Filesystem paths cannot escape the configured root, no path segment of a filesystem key can end with a suffix the backend reserves for metadata or temporary files, unbound logical buckets fail closed, binding prefixes remain within their provider mapping, and each HTTP backend owns its transport lifecycle.

The constrained wrapper enforces registered MIME and byte limits: it rejects a known oversized body before backend I/O, refuses a known-length body that grows before the backend has all of it, and bounds other bodies while streaming. The plugin backend applies it to logical bucket names. A reported rejection deletes nothing, so a rejected overwrite keeps the previous object; a truncated object a backend reported as stored is deleted best-effort. A signed PUT URL enforces the MIME allowlist only.
Remote control operations honor bounded request contexts, but Get returns a caller-owned body whose continued streaming is not cut off by a method-scoped timeout.
Signed URLs are issued only by a capable backend and, for managed bindings, only when the binding explicitly grants signedUrls.
